hints: Choose two array positions and store their sum together with both original indices.
Before searching pairs ending later, look for target minus the current pair sum among sums made by earlier positions.
Only combine pairs with disjoint positions; otherwise one array element could be used twice.
analogy: Save sums from earlier pairs, then ask whether the current pair needs a matching saved sum.
algorithm: For each middle index j, test pairs (j,k) with k>j against sums stored from pairs (i,l) where i<l<j; after tests, add all pairs ending at j. Store representative indices to reconstruct four distinct positions.
correctness: The lookup pair ends before j while the current pair starts at j, so positions cannot overlap; every valid four-index combination is found at its split.
example: For values [1,2,3,4] and target 10, choose all four distinct positions: 1+2+3+4=10.
